Why is the PUCT conducting this survey? Why is the PUCT reopening this survey? What is the deadline for completing this survey? Who should complete this survey? Will signing up to complete this survey constitute official, legal registration with the PUCT as a data center or virtual currency mining facility? How is the PUCT's survey different from the Texas Water Development Board's (TWDB) Annual Water Use Survey? Why does the survey ask questions about power usage in addition to water usage? What will the PUCT do with the data collected in the survey? Are survey responses confidential? What is the process for handling requests for survey data under the Public Information Act? What should you do if you need to edit information that has already been submitted? Will respondents receive a copy of the completed survey to track the information submitted? Is any assistance available for clarification of survey questions? Are all survey questions required to be answered to submit a response? What if questions still remain after reading this guide? Why is the PUCT conducting this survey? The 89th Texas Legislature directed the PUCT to collect data to study the water use of certain industries that have an inverse relationship between energy and water usage (see General Appropriations Act at VIII-57 "Study to Address Water and Emerging Technologies"). The PUCT is conducting this one-time survey to fulfill the legislative requirement and collect data to inform the Texas Water Development Board's (TWDB) statewide water plan. Why is the PUCT reopening this survey At the direction of the House Committee on Natural Resources, the PUCT will be reopening its survey to collect additional responses from data centers and virtual currency mining facilities. The survey will reopen on July 1, 2026, and will be available on the PUCT website. Survey responses are due by July 10, 2026. What is the deadline for completing this survey? Surveys are due by July 10, 2026. Who should complete this survey? The Energy and Water Use survey should be completed by a representative of any data center or virtual currency mining facility that is currently operating or planning to operate in Texas by 2030. For the purpose of this survey, a data center or a virtual currency mining facility consists of one or more buildings located on a single parcel of land or contiguous parcels of land that are either owned or leased by the same entity. If the company has multiple facilities on a single parcel of land or contiguous parcels of land, only one survey response aggregating all units at that facility should be submitted. If a survey was submitted during the original survey period (April 2, 2026 – May 28, 2026), there is no need to resubmit the survey. If survey responses need to be updated from the initial submittal period, please reach out to [email protected] for assistance. Will signing up to complete this survey constitute official, legal registration with the PUCT as a data center or virtual currency mining facility? No. Respondents must sign up to generate facility IDs with unique links to the survey questions. As they sign-up, respondents will provide the number of facilities they will submit surveys for, and each individual facility will be assigned its own facility ID and survey link. The PUCT will not use survey sign-up information outside of this study. PUCT Rule 25.114(c) requires virtual currency mining facilities to register and periodically renew their registration with the PUCT. (Find more information on registration here .) Responding to this survey does not fulfill §25.114(c) requirements to register or renew. How is the PUCT's survey different from the Texas Water Development Board's (TWDB) Annual Water Use Survey? TWDB's survey is limited to questions about actual water use and water sources. The PUCT's survey is designed to collect information on both water use and power use and focused only on data centers and virtual currency mining facilities. TWDB is statutorily directed to provide planning and financial assistance for the development and management of water resources in Texas. The TWDB's annual Water Use Survey was created to collect annual data on water use in Texas to support this directive for state and regional water planning, modeling, and resource management. Why does the survey ask questions about power usage in addition to water usage? The survey includes questions about power use to understand the relationship between energy and water use at these facilities. Cooling technologies used to discharge heat from data centers and virtual currency mining facilities are primarily water‐based or air‐based. As a result, there may exist an inverse relationship between a facility's electricity consumption and its associated water useâ€”e.g., facilities that rely more on water for cooling may use less electricity, while those that rely more on air may require more electricity. The PUCT is collecting information on power use to help explain this inverse relationship with water demand and support more accurate long‐term water planning for Texas. What will the PUCT do with the data collected in the survey? The PUCT is required to share collected data with the TWDB and the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ). The PUCT is also required to prepare a report to submit to the Legislative Budget Board and the Governor by December 31, 2026. Are survey responses confidential? The final report will not include any identifiable information from specific facilities. However, all survey data and responsive information are subject to the requirements of the Texas Public Information Act (PIA, Texas Government Code Chapter 552), including legislative privilege requests under § 552.008. What is the process for handling requests for survey data under the Public Information Act? If survey data or responsive information is requested, the PUCT will take reasonable steps to secure confidential information that is not subject to public disclosure in a public information request. The PUCT will notify the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) and any third party whose interest may be affected by the request. Questions regarding the PIA and how it may apply to survey data and responsive information can be directed to [email protected] . What should you do if you need to edit information that has already been submitted? The form containing survey questions does not allow submitted information to be edited. However, facility ID links may be used to submit updated or corrected information for a facility. If a company reuses a facility ID link to submit revised information, please send an email to [email protected] to notify PUCT staff that an updated filing has been submitted. Will respondents receive a copy of the completed survey to track the information submitted? Yes. Upon submitting the survey, respondents will receive an email confirmation with a copy of the completed survey. Is any assistance available for clarification of survey questions? Several terms and metrics are defined within the survey, in most cases in the text above or near the question. Please reach out to the PUCT at [email protected] if further clarification is needed on survey questions or terms. Are all survey questions required to be answered to submit a response? If some questions cannot be answered, provide an explanation either in the space provided next to the question or under the last question in the survey. What if questions still remain after reading this guide?
